title: Two Del Rio crashes: Willingham and the MJ-12 El Indio-Guerrero case
place_text: Del Rio, Texas / El Indio-Guerrero, Mexico

tellings.quote: >> which that's a huge can of worms because there's two crashes there. 1955 Robert Willingham in Del Rio, Texas and the 1954 Del 1950 Del Rio crash which is actually Elindio/g Guerrero, Texas, Mexico, which is only really talked about in the Eisenhower briefing document of the Majestic 12 documents.

plain: A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels that two separate crashes get linked to Del Rio, Texas: one in 1955 that involved a man named Robert Willingham, and an earlier one in 1950 that really happened at El Indio-Guerrero on the Texas-Mexico border. He says the 1950 crash is mainly discussed in one disputed source, a briefing paper for president-elect Dwight Eisenhower dated 1952 that turned up anonymously on a roll of film in 1984. That paper says "On 06 December, 1950, a second object, probably of similar origin, impacted the earth at high speed in the El Indio - Guerrero area," that it was almost totally burned up, and that what could be recovered was sent to the Atomic Energy Commission's facility at Sandia, New Mexico, for study. The 1950 crash holds only as far as the paper is genuine, which is in dispute, and the paper says nothing about Willingham's 1955 case.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper's page 5 says "On 06 December, 1950, a second object, probably of similar origin, impacted the earth at high speed in the El Indio - Guerrero area of the Texas - Mexican boder" ("boder" as typed), that it was almost totally incinerated, and that "Such material as could be recovered was transported to the A.E.C. facility at Sandia, New Mexico, for study." The teller places the 1950 crash where the paper does and names the paper as its main source, so the crash stands as far as the paper does; the paper says nothing of Willingham's 1955 case, which rests on other tellings.
